Practise variables, conditions, loops, methods, classes, objects and lists before using the advanced units.

Open interactive lesson and complete code

What you are building

Your first console student register

Store a name and mark, choose a pass message and print a list of marks. This is the starting point for the student register learning journey.

All values are temporary and live in memory while the console app runs.

Check the result

Run the program, compare the seven output lines, then change mark to 45 and predict the new messages.

Start with a console student register

You are building a small program that remembers a student name and mark, decides whether the mark is a pass and prints the result. It runs in a text window. Later lessons turn the student idea into an API and a website. Those projects have their own files; do not paste this console Program.cs into an API.

Set up and run

  1. Install Visual Studio with .NET 10 support. Download this lesson's project and extract it.
  2. Open StudyLab.csproj. Choose Build > Build Solution, then Debug > Start Without Debugging.
  3. For a terminal, open the folder containing StudyLab.csproj and run dotnet run.

Understand the pieces

A variable holds a value. A condition chooses which steps run. A loop repeats steps. A method groups steps so you can use them again. A class describes data and behaviour; an object is one instance of that class. A list holds several items.

Read mark >= 50 as "mark is at least 50". A single = assigns a value; == compares values. Braces group steps. A comment begins with // and explains the code to a person.

Expected output

Lefa: 65
Pass
Mark: 65
Mark: 40
Mark: 80
Pass
Student: Lefa, result: Pass

The first decision prints Pass. The loop prints all three list values. The reusable method also returns Pass for 65.

Try it yourself

What changes if mark becomes 45?

The first line shows 45. The decision and method results become Try again. The separate list still prints 65, 40 and 80.

How can the list contain a fourth mark?

Call marks.Add(55); before the foreach loop. The loop will print a fourth line: Mark: 55.

Predict and practise

If mark is 45, will the program print Pass or Try again?

Check your prediction

Try again. The condition 45 >= 50 is false. The list values do not change.

Make one change

Add 55 to the marks list before the loop.

Worked guidance

Insert marks.Add(55); before foreach. Expect one extra Mark: 55 line.

Try independently

Create a second Student with a different name and mark. Print its result using ResultFor.
